emergencyNumber: 112 (emergency line — coverage varies), 199 (fire), 767 (police). In Lagos: 112 or 767
healthcareSystem: Mixed public-private system. Public healthcare is underfunded. Private hospitals in Lagos and Abuja offer better care. Rural healthcare is very limited.
qualityNotes: Private hospitals in Lagos and Abuja offer reasonable care. Public hospitals are overcrowded and under-resourced. For serious medical emergencies, evacuation to South Africa, Europe, or the US may be necessary. Bring all medications you may need.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in cities open 8am-9pm. Limited options outside major cities. Be cautious of counterfeit medications from unregistered vendors.
pharmacyTips: Buy medications only from registered pharmacies (look for Pharmacists Council of Nigeria registration). Counterfeit medications are a serious problem in Nigeria. Major pharmacy chains include HealthPlus and MedPlus. Bring essential medications from home.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is inconsistent. Many medications available without prescription. However, drug quality is a concern — buy from reputable pharmacies only.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing cough syrup
restrictedMeds.note: Banned since 2018 due to abuse epidemic. Not available in Nigeria.

restrictedMeds.name: Tramadol (high dose >100mg)
restrictedMeds.note: High-dose tramadol banned. Low-dose available by prescription.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring sufficient supply for your entire trip — availability is unreliable. Be aware of counterfeit medication risks.

travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance with medical evacuation coverage is ESSENTIAL. Serious medical cases often require evacuation to South Africa or Europe. Ensure your policy covers malaria treatment and emergency air evacuation ($50,000+). Some insurers charge higher premiums for Nigeria.

required: Yellow Fever (required for all travelers — must have valid certificate)
recommended: Meningococcal meningitis (especially during dry season in the north)
Malaria prophylaxis (essential — Nigeria has the highest malaria burden globally)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow Fever vaccination is REQUIRED for all travelers. Malaria is endemic throughout Nigeria — prophylaxis is strongly recommended. Nigeria carries the world's highest malaria burden. Lassa fever occurs in rural areas.

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink anywhere in Nigeria. Use only bottled or filtered water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice in drinks. Sachet water ('pure water') from reputable brands is widely available and affordable.
foodSafetyTips: Eat at established restaurants. Avoid raw vegetables and salads outside of international hotels. Thoroughly cooked street food (suya, jollof rice) from busy vendors is generally safer. Peel all fruits yourself. Use hand sanitizer frequently.
medicalTourismNote: Nigeria is not a medical tourism destination. Many Nigerians travel to India, South Africa, or the UK for specialized medical treatment.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Nigeria. Emergency number 112, yellow fever vaccination required, malaria prevention essential, pharmacy safety tips, and medical evacuation insurance.

hospitals.name: Reddington Hospital
hospitals.notes: Leading private hospital in Lagos. Modern facilities. International standard care.

hospitals.name: Lagoon Hospital (Eko Hospital Group)
hospitals.notes: Major private hospital near business and tourist areas. 24/7 emergency.

hospitals.name: National Hospital Abuja
hospitals.notes: Nigeria's national referral hospital. Located in the capital.

dentalCare.availability: Dental care available in Lagos and Abuja. Quality varies significantly.
dentalCare.costRange: NGN 10,000-50,000 ($6-30) for consultation; NGN 20,000-150,000 ($12-90) for procedures
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Lagos offer decent care. Verify credentials and sterilization practices.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Hospital emergency departments handle dental emergencies. DentPro and Dental Clinic Lagos are reputable options.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Available in Lagos and Abuja. English is the official language.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited but growing. Stigma around mental health remains. Private therapists available in Lagos.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is very limited throughout Nigeria. Infrastructure is challenging for wheelchair users.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Private hospitals in Lagos have some accessibility features. Most facilities lack proper access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Private cars with drivers are the best option.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Lagos traffic can be extreme — plan medical appointments with significant travel time. Many buildings lack elevators and ramps. International hotels are more accessible.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements.
covidStatus.testing: Available at private hospitals and NCDC labs.
covidStatus.notes: Malaria, typhoid, and waterborne diseases are far more common health concerns for travelers.

insuranceClaimProcess: Hospitals require upfront payment (cash or card). Keep all receipts. Private hospitals can provide English documentation. Medical evacuation insurance is critical — verify your policy covers Nigeria specifically.
